stages.name: Protectionism and equality
stages.title: Protectionism and equality
stages.sub: After this, the student can explain why tariffs hit poorer households harder than richer ones.

steps.q: A rich household and a poor household both spend £20 a month more on food because of a tariff. The poor household earns £800 a month, the rich household earns £8,000 a month. Whose income takes the bigger hit, as a proportion?
steps.hint: Compare £20 out of £800 with £20 out of £8,000.

steps.q: A government puts a tariff on imported clothing. Does the shop charge poor customers a different price from rich customers for the same item?
steps.right: No, everyone pays the same higher price
steps.hint: Think about how a tariff changes the price tag in the shop, not who is standing at the till.

steps.q: Given that everyone faces the same price rise, but that price rise takes a bigger slice out of a poor household's income than a rich one's, whose living standards fall by more?
